James Talarico (Democratic), U.S. Senate candidate in Texas: Campaign platform calls for regulations that hold AI companies accountable while protecting workers, for AI companies to follow the same copyright laws as everyone else, and for limits on invasive workplace AI surveillance.
James Talarico (Democratic), U.S. Senate candidate in Texas: Proposed an "AI dividend" to give ordinary people a share of the profits of companies developing AI. No implementation details were given.

Connecticut SB 2 (2024), "An Act Concerning Artificial Intelligence" (2024 session). Sponsors: James Maroney (Democratic). Status: failed on 2024-04-24.  What it does: Comprehensive AI standards bill. Passed the Senate 24-12 along party lines; the House Speaker did not call it for a vote after Gov. Lamont said he would veto it.

Connecticut SB 2 (2025), "An Act Concerning Artificial Intelligence (revised)" (2025 session). Sponsors: James Maroney (Democratic). Status: failed on 2025.  What it does: Revised version of the 2024 comprehensive AI bill, including algorithmic-discrimination duties. Passed the Senate but was not taken up in the House after Gov. Lamont threatened a veto.

Connecticut SB 5 (Public Act 26-15), "Connecticut AI Responsibility and Transparency (CART) Act" (2026 session). Sponsors: James Maroney (Democratic), Martin Looney (Democratic), Bob Duff (Democratic), Saud Anwar (Democratic). Status: enacted on 2026-05-27. Passed the Senate 32-4 and the House 131-17; signed May 27, 2026 (some sources give June 2). What it does: Broad AI law: using an automated employment decision tool is no defense to a discrimination claim; rules for consumer chatbots and AI companions; whistleblower protections and reporting channels at frontier-model developers; AI content provenance; protections for minors. Provisions phase in from Oct. 1, 2026 to 2028.

Connecticut To be filed, "Statewide moratorium on AI data centers" (2027 session (announced)). Sponsors: Bob Duff (Democratic). Status: announced on 2026-10-22. Announced Oct. 22, 2026; not yet filed. What it does: Senate Majority Leader Bob Duff plans to introduce a statewide moratorium on AI data centers when the 2027 session begins, citing their water and electricity use and the effect on utility rates. Some towns, such as East Lyme, have passed local bans.

European Union Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, "EU Artificial Intelligence Act" (European Union). Sponsors: Adopted by the European Parliament and the Council.. Status: enacted on 2024-08-01. In force since Aug. 1, 2024; obligations apply in phases. What it does: Risk-based rules for AI across the EU: bans on certain uses, duties for high-risk systems and for general-purpose AI models, applied in phases. Member states such as France implement and enforce it rather than deciding whether to regulate.

France Government announcement, "Nuclear power for AI data centers" (Government). Sponsors: Emmanuel Macron (Renaissance). Status: announced on 2025-02. Government policy, not a bill. What it does: France pledged a gigawatt of nuclear power for AI computing; in March 2026 President Macron said France's nuclear plants let it open data centers and grow its computing capacity.

Michigan HB 5594-5596, "Statewide data center moratorium (bipartisan House package)" (2025-2026 session). Sponsors: Jennifer Wortz (Republican), Joseph Fox (Republican), Dylan Wegela (Democratic). Michigan SB 1018-1020, "Moratorium on certain approvals for and operation of new data centers" (2025-2026 session). Sponsors: Jim Runestad (Republican), Ruth Johnson (Republican). What it does: Senate package placing a moratorium on certain approvals for, and the operation of, new data centers.

Michigan HB 5396 (with HB 5397-5398), "Repeal of data center sales and use tax exemptions" (2025-2026 session). Sponsors: Dylan Wegela (Democratic). Status: introduced on 2025-12-17. Texas HB 149, "Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (TRAIGA)" (89th Legislature, Regular Session (2025)). Sponsors: Giovanni Capriglione (Republican). Status: enacted on 2025-06-22. Signed June 22, 2025; effective Jan. 1, 2026. What it does: Bans a short list of AI uses, including AI-generated child sexual abuse material and government social scoring, and requires Texas state agencies to disclose AI use to consumers. A broader high-risk impact-assessment regime in early drafts was cut from the final bill.

Texas SB 293 (also HB 167), "Repeal of the data center sales tax exemption" (90th Legislature (2027), prefiled). Sponsors: Joan Huffman (Republican), Trey Martinez Fischer (Democratic). Status: introduced on 2026-11-09. Filed Nov. 9, 2026. What it does: Would end existing data center sales tax breaks. SB 293 reportedly has 23 Senate authors; HB 167 is a House bill with the same aim.

Texas SB 33, SB 35, SB 36, "Data center cost, water-reporting and local-incentive bills" (90th Legislature (2027), prefiled). Sponsors: Judith Zaffirini (Democratic). Status: introduced on 2026-11-09. Filed Nov. 9, 2026. What it does: SB 33: data centers may not raise electricity costs for Texas residents. SB 35: large data centers report water use to the Texas Water Development Board. SB 36: no new local tax incentives for data centers.

U.S. federal Number to verify, "GRID Savings Act" (119th Congress (2025-2026)). Sponsors: Martin Heinrich (Democratic). Status: introduced. Status to verify. What it does: Would direct federal regulators to require large electricity customers such as data centers to pay for the infrastructure needed to connect them to the grid.

U.S. federal H.R. 3447, "Chip Security Act" (119th Congress (2025-2026)). Sponsors: Bill Huizenga (Republican), Bill Foster (Democratic). Status: in-committee on 2026-03-26. Ordered reported 42-0 by House Foreign Affairs; reportedly included in the Senate FY2027 NDAA. What it does: Would require advanced AI chips to carry security mechanisms that verify their location.

U.S. federal H.R. 6875, "AI OVERWATCH Act" (119th Congress (2025-2026)). Sponsors: Sponsors to verify.. Status: in-committee on 2026-01-21. Ordered reported 42-2 by House Foreign Affairs; reportedly included in the Senate FY2027 NDAA. What it does: Would require the administration to notify Congress before approving advanced chip exports and let Congress block them.

U.S. federal H.R. 8170, "MATCH Act" (119th Congress (2025-2026)). Sponsors: Sponsors to verify.. Status: in-committee on 2026-04-22. Ordered reported 36-8 by House Foreign Affairs; reportedly included in the Senate FY2027 NDAA. What it does: Would require allied nations to match U.S. controls on exports of advanced chipmaking equipment to China.

U.S. federal H.R. 9442, "Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act" (119th Congress (2025-2026)). Sponsors: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (Democratic). Status: in-committee on 2026-06-24. Introduced June 24, 2026; referred to committee. What it does: House companion to S. 4214, with about 20 cosponsors. Referred to the Energy and Commerce and Foreign Affairs committees.

U.S. federal S. 4214, "Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act" (119th Congress (2025-2026)). Sponsors: Bernie Sanders (Independent). Status: in-committee on 2026-03-25. Introduced Mar. 25, 2026; referred to committee. What it does: Would prohibit building or upgrading AI data centers until laws regulating AI and AI data centers are enacted. Referred to the Senate Commerce Committee.

U.S. federal Number to verify, "States' Right to Regulate AI Act" (119th Congress (2025-2026)). Sponsors: Ed Markey (Democratic). Status: introduced on 2025-12.  What it does: Would bar the use of federal funds to carry out the December 2025 executive order targeting state AI laws.

U.S. federal Take It Down Act, "Take It Down Act" (119th Congress (2025-2026)). Sponsors: Ted Cruz (Republican), Amy Klobuchar (Democratic). Status: enacted on 2025-05-19.  What it does: Makes it a federal crime to publish or threaten to publish non-consensual intimate images, including AI deepfakes; platforms must remove flagged content within 48 hours.
